notes: In 3.2, container-test-result-export replaces publish-test-results-execution-boundary to test a less obvious task boundary. code-coverage-pipeline-completion-timing replaces test-results-code-coverage-boundary because supported publishing scenarios can include coverage. test-results-publication-failure-policy replaces test-results-run-merging to avoid a setting-name giveaway.

cards.statement: Publishers send new Azure Artifacts package versions directly to the @release view.
cards.explanation: Publish packages to the base feed, then promote chosen versions to @release.
cards.misconception: A release view is a publication endpoint.

cards.statement: Azure Artifacts automatically saves upstream packages a Feed and Upstream Reader (Collaborator) installs via the feed.
cards.explanation: The Feed and Upstream Reader (Collaborator) role includes saving installed upstream packages into the feed.

cards.statement: Azure Artifacts checks upstream sources before packages published directly to the feed.
cards.explanation: Azure Artifacts checks directly published packages, then saved upstream packages, then packages available upstream.
cards.misconception: Configured upstream sources take precedence over locally published packages.

cards.statement: Azure Artifacts keeps a version reserved after you delete the published package.
cards.explanation: Azure Artifacts keeps a deleted package's version reserved. Publish changed contents under a new version.

cards.statement: Azure Artifacts feed views identify whether a package change breaks API compatibility.
cards.explanation: Azure Artifacts views communicate validation quality. SemVer communicates the nature and risk of a change.
cards.misconception: Feed views carry the compatibility meaning of semantic version numbers.

cards.statement: Azure Pipelines automatically resets $(Rev:r) when a date-based run number's date changes.
cards.explanation: Azure Pipelines restarts the revision when the date changes in a run number such as $(Date:yyyyMMdd).$(Rev:r).

cards.statement: GitHub Packages adopts repository permissions by default when you link an already published container package.
cards.explanation: Linking a published package in GitHub Packages preserves existing access rules. Enable inheritance to adopt repository access.
cards.misconception: Linking a published package automatically switches its access rules to the repository's.

cards.statement: Azure Artifacts can accept a new publication of a version present in an enabled upstream source.
cards.explanation: For Azure Artifacts, disable the relevant upstream before publishing a version it already contains; re-enable it afterward.
cards.misconception: An enabled upstream permits local publication of its existing package versions.

cards.statement: Azure Pipelines can retrieve a pipeline artifact version from a specified producing run.
cards.explanation: Azure Pipelines binds pipeline artifacts to their producing run. Select that run to retrieve its artifact version.

cards.statement: Microsoft recommends upstreams with internally customized OSS ahead of public registries in Azure Artifacts.
cards.explanation: Microsoft's Azure Artifacts guidance puts public registries first, except that an upstream with internally customized OSS packages takes priority.

cards.statement: Azure Pipelines' Publish Test Results task extracts results from a Docker build image.
cards.explanation: For tests executed during a Docker build, export result files to the pipeline host before publishing them.
cards.misconception: Test-result publishing extracts files stored in a built container image directly.

cards.statement: Azure Pipelines' Visual Studio Test task can balance test slices using past execution times.
cards.explanation: Execution-time slicing groups tests so each slice has approximately equal expected duration across the agents.

source.title: Run tests in parallel using the Visual Studio Test task

cards.statement: Azure Pipelines shows Code Coverage tab results while deployment stages run in a multistage YAML pipeline.
cards.explanation: The Code Coverage tab's results become available after the whole multistage YAML pipeline completes, delaying that coverage review until the run ends.
cards.misconception: A completed build stage exposes the Code Coverage tab's results while downstream stages remain active.
cards.volatilityNote: The timing of coverage reporting can change as Azure Pipelines evolves.

source.title: Review and configure code coverage results in Azure Pipelines

cards.statement: Azure Load Testing can fail a CI/CD run when a response-time fail criterion is met.
cards.explanation: A performance threshold in the load test configuration determines the test status, and the CI/CD run reflects that result.

source.title: Define fail criteria for load tests by using Azure Load Testing

cards.statement: Azure Load Testing can execute a k6 script as a pipeline's load test.
cards.explanation: Azure Load Testing runs Apache JMeter or Locust scripts; k6 scripts use another test framework.
cards.misconception: Azure Load Testing accepts k6 scripts as well as its supported framework scripts.
cards.volatilityNote: The frameworks supported by Azure Load Testing can expand.

cards.statement: Azure Pipelines runs the Manual Validation task in an agentless job.
cards.explanation: The Manual Validation task pauses a YAML run within a stage and executes in a server job rather than occupying an agent.

cards.statement: Azure Pipelines Test Impact Analysis includes newly added tests in its selected test set.
cards.explanation: Test Impact Analysis includes new tests in its selection so incremental validation exercises tests introduced by the change.

source.title: Speed up testing by using Test Impact Analysis

cards.statement: Azure Pipelines requires an interactive process for visible UI tests on self-hosted Windows agents.
cards.explanation: Visible UI tests run on self-hosted Windows agents configured as interactive processes with autologon, providing an accessible desktop session.

cards.statement: Azure Pipelines fails the Publish Test Results task by default when a reported test fails.
cards.explanation: The Publish Test Results task publishes failing outcomes by default. Enable failTaskOnFailedTests to make reported failures fail the task.
cards.misconception: Publishing a failed test outcome fails the publication task under its default settings.

cards.statement: Azure Pipelines' Query Azure Monitor Alerts check succeeds when a matching alert is active.
cards.explanation: Query Azure Monitor Alerts succeeds when none of the queried alert rules are activated at evaluation time.
cards.misconception: A successful alert query means that the health check succeeds even when it finds an active alert.

cards.statement: Azure Pipelines assigns a fresh virtual machine per job using Microsoft-hosted agents.
cards.explanation: A Microsoft-hosted job starts with clean machine state; local changes from an earlier job stay with that earlier machine.

cards.statement: Microsoft-hosted agents can reach a corporate network through its ExpressRoute private connection.
cards.explanation: Microsoft-hosted agents contact corporate servers over public networking. ExpressRoute and VPN connections do not give these agents a private route.
cards.misconception: Hosted agents use the organization's private Azure network connections.

cards.statement: Managed DevOps Pools can provision agents from custom generalized Azure Compute Gallery images.
cards.explanation: An engineer selects a generalized image from Azure Compute Gallery when the pool needs a prepared software environment.

cards.statement: The Azure Pipelines GitHub App runs builds as the GitHub user who installs the app.
cards.explanation: GitHub App authentication runs builds and reports status under the Azure Pipelines identity, rather than the installer's personal identity.
cards.misconception: The GitHub App delegates builds to its installer's personal identity.

cards.statement: Azure Pipelines adds explicit GitHub branch triggers to the pipeline's existing implicit CI trigger.
cards.explanation: An explicit trigger replaces Azure Pipelines' implicit CI trigger for a GitHub repository; configured branch filters determine which pushes start runs.
cards.misconception: Explicit branch filters supplement the implicit trigger instead of replacing it.

cards.statement: Azure Pipelines schedules independent jobs within a stage for parallel execution by default.
cards.explanation: The YAML list's job order supplies no execution dependency; dependencies need explicit configuration.

cards.statement: Azure Pipelines can reevaluate ${{ }} expressions after a task changes a variable in the same run.
cards.explanation: Azure Pipelines resolves template expressions while it compiles the YAML plan. Task-time variable updates leave those resolved values unchanged.
cards.misconception: Template expressions refresh their values during task execution.

cards.statement: Azure Pipelines can enforce an extends relationship through a resource's required template check.
cards.explanation: The required template check verifies that the pipeline extends the named template; including that file inserts content but does not meet the check.

cards.statement: Azure Pipelines reads an environment's approvals and checks from the pipeline author's YAML file.
cards.explanation: Resource administrators configure approvals and checks separately from YAML. Editing the pipeline file leaves the environment's check configuration intact.
cards.misconception: Pipeline authors define environment approvals and checks in YAML.

cards.statement: Azure Pipelines checks a secret-bearing variable group's authorization for the consuming pipeline.
cards.explanation: Naming a secret-bearing variable group in YAML does not authorize its use; the pipeline needs a matching library authorization.

cards.statement: Azure Pipelines deployment jobs inherit the implicit checkout: self behavior of regular jobs.
cards.explanation: Azure Pipelines uses checkout: none when a deployment job omits checkout. Add checkout: self to fetch the pipeline's source repository.
cards.misconception: Deployment jobs receive the same implicit source checkout as ordinary jobs.

cards.statement: Azure Pipelines injects artifact downloads into a deployment job's deploy hook by default.
cards.explanation: The deploy lifecycle hook receives an implicit artifact download step. Set download: none in that hook when the deployment uses another artifact source.

cards.statement: Azure Pipelines accepts the rolling strategy for Kubernetes resources in an environment.
cards.explanation: Azure Pipelines rolling deployments target virtual machine resources. A Kubernetes environment resource does not enable that deployment-job strategy.
cards.misconception: The rolling deployment-job strategy works with Kubernetes environment resources.

cards.statement: Azure Pipelines combines deployments from multiple pipelines in an environment's deployment history.
cards.explanation: An environment's deployment record identifies the pipeline and run behind a change, so releases from separate services remain traceable together.

source.title: Create and target Azure DevOps environments for pipelines

cards.statement: Azure Pipelines repeats configured postRouteTraffic health checks at successive canary increments.
cards.explanation: Azure Pipelines repeats the canary lifecycle hooks as exposure grows. A failing health-check step can stop progression and enter the failure path.

cards.statement: Azure Pipelines defaults postRouteTraffic to a server job for deployments that use an agent pool.
cards.explanation: Azure Pipelines runs lifecycle hooks in the deployment job's pool unless the hook sets another pool. A postRouteTraffic health check follows that inherited setting.
cards.misconception: Post-deployment health-check hooks select an agentless server job implicitly.

cards.statement: Azure Front Door can switch production traffic between parallel AKS clusters in a blue-green rollout.
cards.explanation: In Microsoft's AKS blue-green pattern, Azure Front Door changes routing after the new cluster passes validation. The current cluster serves traffic during preparation.

cards.statement: The application defines the groups evaluated by Azure App Configuration's targeting filter.
cards.explanation: An application's groups can represent rollout stages or locations as well as Microsoft Entra groups. The targeting filter uses the groups the application supplies.

source.title: Roll out features to targeted audiences

cards.statement: Azure App Configuration lets percentage allocation override explicit user assignments in variant flags.
cards.explanation: A variant's explicit user or group assignment overrides its percentage allocation. A named tester can receive the selected variant regardless of the allocation bucket.
cards.misconception: Percentage allocations outrank named user overrides in variant feature flags.

cards.statement: Azure Pipelines starts an application stage under its default condition after its database stage dependency fails.
cards.explanation: The default Azure Pipelines stage condition expects its dependencies to succeed. An application stage therefore skips when its database deployment dependency fails.
cards.misconception: Waiting for a dependency to finish is sufficient for the default stage condition, regardless of its outcome.
